newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up at three-year high.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up at three-year high.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up sharply on Monday, hitting its highest level since January 20, 1994, with institutions seen particularly targetting blue-chip stocks, brokers said.
But the index was pulled off its highs by some profit-taking from retail investors later in the afternoon, they added.
The B index surged 3.013 points or 3.56 percent to 87.530 points on volume of 69.417 million shares worth $36.359 million, compared with $35.762 million on Friday.
"The market tone is bullish, but it is likely to take a rest around the current level before another run up towards 100 points," said one broker.
"Technical charts show some signs of over-buying after the surges of the past few sessions," another broker said. "A correction is needed at this level."
All 43 B shares traded, with 37 up, four flat and two down.
Shanghai Friendship & Overseas Chinese was the star on its 1996 dividend and bonus issue plans, surging $0.054 or 9.89 percent to $0.600 on volume of 3.0 million shares.
Shanghai Chlor Alkai was the most actively traded share on institutional buying, gaining $0.006 or 1.81 percent to $0.336 on volume of 3.9 million shares.
The Shanghai A share index ended firmer on bullish sentiment, but is probably heading for a correction in the short term, brokers said.
The index rose 24.500 points or 1.75 percent to 1,424.106 points on volume of 11.8 billion shares worth 13.2 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index climbed 86.049 points or 2.39 percent to 3,682.336 points.
Hebei Weiyuan Industry was the best performer on speculative buying, surging 0.99 yuan or 10.05 percent to 10.84 yuan on volume of 4.5 million shares.
